beats.speaker: narration
beats.text: Riley lays three cards face down. "Let's see the whole shape of this, not just today's."

beats.prompt: The past: the collapse that cleared the ground you're standing on now.
The present: the dream, and the call you finally picked up.
The future: the answer you just gave, out loud, for the first time.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Okay, quiz me. If this is supposedly my vocation, why did it take a total collapse and a bad dream to get here?"

options.text: Because rebirth doesn't skip the ending — it needs one to actually happen.
It means the vocation isn't real, since it came from a mess.
The path getting here doesn't matter at all.

elaboration: Rebirth requires passing through an ending first — the collapse and the dream weren't detours, they were the road.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "What if this is just relief talking, and not an actual calling?"

options.text: A real calling and real relief aren't opposites — this can be both at once.
Relief means it's fake, throw it out.
Feelings are irrelevant to whether a calling is real.

elaboration: A calling being answered is exactly this: your true vocation coming into focus, whatever else you happen to feel alongside it.

beats.speaker: narration
beats.text: "One thread ties all three: the ground that had to come down, the dream that made you look, and the voice you just decided, finally, to use."

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Yeah. I'm not saying I've got it figured out — I don't. But for the first time in years, this actually feels like mine, start to finish. That's enough to build on."
